robot-tells.title: The Robot Tells
robot-tells.subtitle: 12 giveaways that prove AI wrote your content, and a 30-second fix for each
intro: People don't need a detector to spot AI writing. They just feel it. The post is smooth, polite, and weirdly empty, so they scroll past.

This checklist shows you the 12 patterns that give it away. Each one has a fast fix and a before/after so you can see it work. Run your next draft through it before you hit post. It takes about two minutes.

tells.name: The throat-clearing opener
tells.spot: The first line talks about the world instead of the point. "In today's fast-paced digital landscape..."
tells.fix: Delete the first sentence. Start with the thing you actually wanted to say.
tells.before: In today's fast-paced digital world, building an audience is more important than ever.
tells.after: Nobody followed me for the first 90 days.

tells.name: "It's not X, it's Y"
tells.spot: A claim set up as a fake contrast. "It's not about posting more. It's about posting better." AI loves this shape.
tells.fix: Say the claim once, plainly, and back it with one fact.
tells.before: It's not about working harder. It's about working smarter.
tells.after: I cut my posts from 7 a week to 3 and got more replies.

tells.name: The perfect triplet
tells.spot: Every list has exactly three tidy items. "Clear, concise, and compelling."
tells.fix: Keep only the item that is actually true. Or use two. Or use four. Break the pattern.
tells.before: Great copy is clear, concise, and compelling.
tells.after: Great copy is clear. That's the whole job.

tells.name: The vocabulary tell
tells.spot: Words real people almost never say out loud: delve, tapestry, leverage, unlock, elevate, game-changer, seamless, robust, navigate the landscape.
tells.fix: Say it the way you'd say it to a friend across the table. Swap each fancy word for the plain one.
tells.before: Let's delve into how you can leverage this game-changing tool.
tells.after: Here's how to use this tool.

tells.name: Em dash overload
tells.spot: Dashes everywhere, holding sentences together that should have been two sentences.
tells.fix: Allow yourself one per post at most. Everywhere else, use a period.
tells.before: The offer is simple, it's fast, and it works, even if you're starting from zero.
tells.after: The offer is simple. It's fast. It works even if you're starting from zero.

tells.name: Fake hype
tells.spot: Cheerful filler: "Let's dive in!" "Buckle up!" "Here's the thing." Energy with no information.
tells.fix: Cut every line that announces what you're about to say. Just say it.
tells.before: Buckle up, because we're about to dive into something amazing!
tells.after: Here's the exact DM I sent.

tells.name: Vague claims
tells.spot: "Many people struggle with..." "Studies show..." No number, no name, no price, no date.
tells.fix: Add one concrete detail: a number, a name, a place, a price, or a day of the week.
tells.before: Many beginners struggle to make their first sale.
tells.after: Most beginners I talk to are 60 days in with $0 and 4 half-built products.

tells.name: Perfect rhythm
tells.spot: Every paragraph is the same length. Every sentence is the same shape. It reads like a metronome.
tells.fix: Break it up. Add a one-line paragraph. Use a fragment. Let one sentence run long and the next stop short.
tells.before: Posting daily builds trust. Trust leads to sales. Sales create growth.
tells.after: Post daily. Trust comes first. Sales come after, sometimes a lot after.

tells.name: The summary closer
tells.spot: "In conclusion..." "Ultimately..." "At the end of the day..." The post repeats itself to feel finished.
tells.fix: End on your last useful point, or on a question you actually want answered.
tells.before: In conclusion, consistency and authenticity are key to long-term success.
tells.after: What's the one post you've been avoiding?

tells.name: Hedging mush
tells.spot: "It's important to note that..." "This can potentially help..." "May improve..." Nothing is ever committed to.
tells.fix: Say it or cut it. If you're not sure, say that you're not sure, and say why.
tells.before: It's important to note that this approach can potentially help improve results.
tells.after: This worked for me. I don't know if it'll work for you.

tells.name: Emoji bullet lists
tells.spot: Every point has a rocket, a checkmark, or a lightbulb, with a bold header, even for a three-line post.
tells.fix: Write sentences. Use at most one emoji, or none.
tells.before:
🚀 Boost engagement
✅ Save time
💡 Grow faster
tells.after: This saves me about an hour a day, and my replies went up.

tells.name: No scars, no opinion
tells.spot: Nothing in the post could only have come from you. No story, no mistake, no opinion that someone might disagree with.
tells.fix: Add one thing that happened to you, with a detail only you would know. Then take a side.
tells.before: Email marketing is a powerful tool for any business.
tells.after: My first email list was 14 people, and 6 were family. I still sent every email like it mattered.

routine: Read the first line out loud. If it talks about "the world" or "today's landscape", delete it.
Search the draft for dashes and fancy words (delve, leverage, unlock, elevate, seamless). Replace them.
Find every vague claim and add one real number, name, or detail.
Make one paragraph shorter than the others. Make one longer.
Cut the last paragraph if it just repeats the post.
Add one sentence only you could have written.
robot-tells.score: Count how many of the 12 tells you find. 0 to 2 reads like a person. 3 to 5 reads like a person using AI, which is fine if the story is yours. 6 or more reads like a robot, and readers will keep scrolling.
robot-tells.closer: The goal is not to hide that you used AI. The goal is to make something worth reading. Fix these 12 and your posts will sound like you again.

ai-word-list.title: The AI Word List
ai-word-list.subtitle: The words that make people reply, call, or buy, and where to put them
intro: Most posts and DMs fail on word choice, not on the offer. A few small words make it easy for someone to say yes. A few others make them feel sold to.
This list gives you words that work, grouped by the job they do, with weak versus stronger examples. Copy them into posts, DMs, subject lines, and sales pages.
One rule goes with all of it: only use a word if it's true. Urgency you invent and promises you can't keep cost you more than they earn.

groups.name: 1. Words that get a reply
groups.job: Use in the first line of a DM or comment. They keep the pressure low and make answering easy.
groups.weak: Hi, I help people grow their business. Interested?
groups.strong: Quick question. Saw your post about your first launch. What's been the hardest part so far?

groups.name: 2. Words that make the promise specific
groups.job: Use in headlines and the first line of a post. Specific beats impressive.
groups.strong: How to get your first $50 sale in 7 days, even if you have no list.

groups.name: 3. Words that lower the risk
groups.job: Use near the button, the price, and the ask. They answer the fear of getting it wrong.
groups.strong: Grab it free. No card needed. Keep it either way.

groups.name: 4. Words that create real urgency
groups.job: Use only when there is a true deadline or limit. Name the date or the number.
groups.weak: Hurry! Don't miss out on this amazing deal!
groups.strong: Price goes up Friday at midnight. After that it's $27.

groups.name: 5. Words that say "this is for you"
groups.job: Use at the top of a post or page. People act when they see themselves in it.
groups.strong: For solo beginners with $0 and no list who want a first sale.

groups.name: 6. Words that show proof
groups.job: Use right after a claim. A claim with a reason beats a claim alone.
groups.strong: I tested it for 14 days. Here's what happened, with the screenshots.

groups.name: 7. Words that name the pain
groups.job: Use in the opening of a post, an email, or a sales page. Describe the problem before you sell the fix.
groups.strong: Posting every day and still getting zero replies?

groups.name: 8. Words that ask for the action
groups.job: Use in the last line. Tell people the one thing to do and make it small.
groups.weak: Let me know if you'd like to learn more.
groups.strong: Reply with the word LIST and I'll send it over.

ai-word-list.cut_intro: These words make your writing sound weak, vague, or like an ad. Search your draft for them and delete or replace.

cut.why: It apologizes. "Just checking in" becomes "Checking in".
Hedging makes people trust you less. Commit or say why you're unsure.
Nobody talks like this. Name the thing you do.
Hype words with no detail. Say what changes.
Adjectives you give yourself don't count. Show a result.
Say what they get. "Get the checklist" beats "Click here".

placement.use: Groups 5, 7, and 2. Make the reader feel seen or promise something specific.
Group 1. Keep it low pressure and about them.
Group 6. Back up every big claim with a reason or a result.
Group 3. Answer the fear of getting it wrong.
Group 8, plus a true Group 4 if there's a real deadline.
Groups 1 and 2. Short, specific, and curious. Under 50 characters.

ai-word-list.prompt_title: Copy and paste this into any AI
ai-word-list.prompt: Rewrite the text below. Use plain words. Cut these words: just, maybe, leverage, unlock, elevate, game-changer, amazing. Start with the reader's problem in one line. Make the promise specific with a number or a time frame. Add one reason it works. End with one small action. Keep my voice. Text: [paste your draft here]
ai-word-list.closer: Start with one group. Rewrite one post or DM using it today. Then check what changes in your replies.
